# Top 100 interview roadmap

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from questions/roadmap.js: do not edit by hand -->

100 problems from the course, grouped by pattern. Each problem is available in the browser (Interview page, with your progress) and locally:

```bash
python dsa.py test <id>
```

## Tracks

| Track | Problems | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Beginner | 24 | Finish topics 1–12 first. Classic easy problems that every interviewer expects you to solve quickly. |
| Intermediate | 56 | The core of phone screens and most onsite rounds: one clear pattern per problem. |
| Advanced | 20 | Hard problems that combine patterns. Aim here once the intermediate track feels routine. |

## Eight-week plan

| Week | Focus |
|---|---|
| Week 1 | Arrays and hashing, two pointers (beginner + intermediate) |
| Week 2 | Sliding window, stack and queue |
| Week 3 | Binary search, linked lists |
| Week 4 | Trees and BSTs |
| Week 5 | Heaps, tries, backtracking |
| Week 6 | Graphs |
| Week 7 | Greedy, intervals, dynamic programming |
| Week 8 | Bits and design; then the advanced track and timed mock interviews |

## How to use it

1. Do the problems of one group in order. Before coding, say the pattern out loud.
2. If you are stuck for 20 minutes, take one hint, not the solution.
3. Mark a problem as done only if you can re-solve it from a blank file a few days later.
4. After each group, do one timed round on the Interview page at the same difficulty.
